item.title: The importance of the change-of-variables integration technique in deriving the PDFs of important probability distributions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this article is to explicitly describe how the integration technique known as the change of variables is used in graduate-level Probability and Statistics courses. Throughout the article, we employ this integration technique seven times across various examples and results. We demonstrate that four applications of this technique are required to derive the probability density function (PDF) of the Student's t-distribution.
item.dc:creator: Jorge P. Arpasi

item.title: A Sharp Norm Inequality and Buzano's Inequality via Determinants
item.description: arXiv:2604.01525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a short linear-algebraic proof of the inequality $$ \|x\|_1\,\|x\|_\infty \le \frac{1+\sqrt{n}}{2}\,\|x\|_2^2, $$ valid for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. This inequality relates three fundamental norms on finite-dimensional spaces and has applications in optimization and numerical analysis. Our proof exploits the determinantal structure of a parametrized family of quadratic forms, and we show the constant $(1+\sqrt{n})/2$ is optimal. The inequality is a special case of Buzano's inequality, and the same method also proves Buzano's inequality for real vectors.
item.dc:creator: Jose Antonio Lara Benitez
